newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore calls for more safety in Malacca Straits.
newsitem.headline: Singapore calls for more safety in Malacca Straits.

text.p: A Singapore minister on Tuesday said more needed to be done to ensure the safety of shipping in the Malacca Straits, a key international route likely to get even busier as Asian trade continues to boom.

Junior Defence Minister Matthias Yao told a maritime conference that although much had been done to regulate shipping and stamp out piracy, safety concerns were growing along with the volume in traffic, now around 200 ships a day.
"Solutions must be found to deal with the problem," he said in a speech prepared for delivery to the conference.
"The search for better measures and arrangements is a continuing process. The littoral states are continually exploring new initiatives," Yao said without giving further details.
He said piracy was still a problem because raiders of ships moving relatively slowly through the Straits could escape pursuit by scurrying into the territorial waters of another nation.
But he said joint patrols set up in 1992 by the Singapore and Indonesian navies, along with a "hot pursuit" agreement, had worked.
In the seven months before the agreement came into force, there were 33 reported piracy cases, Yao said.
"Since the inception in 1992, the area has been virtually free of sea robbery," he said.
